# v3.0.0

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **Settings are now loaded from `config.yml`; `settings.ini` is no longer read.**
  Move your existing settings from `settings.ini` into `config.yml` before upgrading,
  or your settings will be silently ignored. (de29b3d)

## Features

- Load settings from `config.yml`. (de29b3d)

## Bug fixes

- Failed uploads are now retried. (29d98d5)

## Performance

- Parsed templates are cached. (b347c26)

## Internal

- Codebase formatted with ruff. (65a2c0b)

I wrote the release notes to `RELEASE_NOTES.md` and labelled the release **v3.0.0**. I haven't committed the file or created a tag.

**Why v3.0.0:** the last tag, `v2.3.1`, points at the initial commit, and one of the four commits since then breaks existing setups. `de29b3d` stops reading `settings.ini` and loads settings from `config.yml` instead. Under semantic versioning, a breaking change means a new major version, so the next release is 3.0.0 rather than 2.4.0.

**What's in the notes:**
- **Breaking changes** (listed first): settings now come from `config.yml`, and users need to move their settings out of `settings.ini` before upgrading.
- **Features:** loading settings from `config.yml`.
- **Bug fixes:** failed uploads are now retried (`29d98d5`).
- **Performance:** parsed templates are cached (`b347c26`).
- **Internal:** code formatted with ruff (`65a2c0b`). You may want to drop this one from user-facing notes.

The repo has no code beyond `history.txt`, so I wrote the notes from the commit messages alone and couldn't check them against the code. In particular, I can't tell whether a leftover `settings.ini` gets ignored silently or causes an error, so the upgrade note just tells users to move their settings. A short example of what goes in `config.yml` would also help users migrate, if you can share the format.
